hints: Translate each value in one permutation to its position in the other.
A common subsequence then becomes an increasing sequence of positions.
Use the standard longest increasing subsequence algorithm with reconstruction.
analogy: The first permutation gives each value a destination rank; keep a longest sequence whose ranks increase.
example: For permutations [2,1,3] and [1,2,3], transformed positions are [2,1,3]; an LIS is [1,3], corresponding to common subsequence [1,3].
algorithm: Build pos[value] from the second permutation, then replace each element of the first by its position. Compute a strictly increasing subsequence using a tails array and lower_bound. Keep the index ending each tail length and a predecessor for every position; follow predecessors from the final tail to reconstruct the actual values.
correctness: A sequence appears in the second permutation in the same order exactly when its mapped positions strictly increase. Thus common subsequences correspond one-to-one to increasing subsequences of the mapped first permutation. The tails algorithm finds the maximum length and predecessor links reconstruct one such sequence.
complexity: For n values, time is O(n log n) and space O(n).
